guide.title: Using PMRS: start, inspect, intervene and deliver
guide.intro: PMRS keeps your exact question, source files, mathematical work and review evidence in a local project. This guide is available inside the application in English and Simplified Chinese. Research and report bodies remain English; quoted original material keeps its original bytes.
guide.setup.title: 1. First launch and setup
guide.setup.1: Open PMRS from Applications. In Settings & sign-in, check the official client and sign-in state, and use the environment check. Select an existing Codex CLI or Tectonic path, or use the offered component setup. Tectonic and its offline resources are needed for formal PDF reports; they are separate from model sign-in.
guide.setup.2: Choose Language at the top of the window. The saved choice survives reopening and port changes. Switching language does not start research or change frozen task inputs. Native operating-system dialogs may use the desktop language.
guide.setup.3: A project stores shared knowledge and material. A named workflow instance binds one target or investigation scope. A round records a concrete purpose and finite authorization. Select the correct project and instance before starting, correcting, reporting or handing off work.
guide.choose.title: 2. Choose TRW, TFDW or Survey
guide.choose.1: TRW studies an exact statement. In New project, select TRW and provide its full objects, domain, assumptions, quantifiers and conclusion. You can paste text or select a UTF-8 problem file. Creating the project saves the original and leaves a paused instance without a model call.
guide.choose.2: TFDW starts from observations. Fill Phenomenon, examples or conjecture family (original text), Immutable background and constraints, and Allowed exploration or changes separately. Say what may vary and what must stay fixed. An incomplete draft must be completed before research starts. Examples alone do not establish a candidate theorem.
guide.choose.3: Survey investigates a topic or existing knowledge. Choose Explore a new topic, Write from existing knowledge, or Update an existing survey. Fill the topic, specific questions, objects, conditions, inclusion and exclusion boundaries. Choose Knowledge only for a knowledge deliverable or Survey manuscript when an English manuscript is intended. These entries create paused instances.
guide.start.title: 3. Authorize and start
guide.start.1: Open Start research round. Enter a specific Round intent, then select Materials for this round (optional selection) and Existing knowledge for this round (optional selection) when needed. Both allow multiple selections. Maximum calls this round defaults to 12 in the web form; CLI start requires an explicit call limit; only advanced plan-work defaults to 8. Maximum concurrent tasks uses the saved project value, initially 1. Submitting authorizes model work; creation, reading and refreshing do not.
guide.start.2: Review model settings before submission. Add or update this scope applies one stage, role and purpose. Configure future tasks in the existing round affects newly frozen tasks; an existing request keeps its original model and inputs. Unsupported capabilities fail explicitly rather than silently changing the model.
guide.start.3: The workflow graph shows duties and actual activity. Selecting a stage opens details; it is not a command to run every stage. Plan research work is an advanced finite-plan control for explicit branches, materials and dependencies. Its Run this authorized plan after saving checkbox defaults off.
guide.observe.title: 4. Observe work and read the evidence
guide.observe.1: Current knowledge contains full statements, arguments and their exact support scope. Open questions contains missing work and unresolved conditions. Tasks & configuration shows each actual task, frozen model policy and request state. Research history retains native events, and Round changes shows additions, reuse, support changes and withdrawals.
guide.observe.2: Progress updates automatically. An update notice lets you choose when to refresh the content list while you read a stable snapshot. Stage highlights mean actual activity, not a percentage of proof completion. A saved record, completed task or accepted response is not mathematical proof; inspect checked and unchecked scope.
guide.observe.3: PREPARED means the exact task is frozen. RESERVED or SENT means its original execution may be in progress. CAPTURED means the original response exists but may still need admission. SETTLED records its admission outcome. UNKNOWN means the send outcome is uncertain; it is never permission to send a replacement automatically.
guide.budget.title: 5. Calls, concurrency and selected materials
guide.budget.1: A call budget is the total authorized work, including research and explicitly requested report roles. Concurrency is how many calls may run together; raising it does not add calls. A project supports 1–8 model slots, while participating PMRS projects share a host pool of 10 according to ready demand. With two ready projects this can be 5/5; with demand of 2 and 8 it can be 2/8. Existing lower project limits remain in force.
guide.budget.2: Tasks also wait for scientific dependencies, short preparation slots, physical memory, disk or rendering resources. Not every available model slot must be used. Independent checks keep their own exact inputs. Report and accounting work receive a scheduling turn after bounded ordinary work rather than being postponed indefinitely.
guide.budget.3: Use Add materials to store sources, then select the material relevant to the actual duty. The project library is shared storage; it is not copied into every request. Each new task keeps references to its necessary target, premises, source bytes and declared evidence. The executor prepares readable files and checks their hashes. Existing frozen tasks keep their original input identity.
guide.budget.4: Oversized inputs stop before sending. The local input support limit is 32 MiB including required unique material and metadata; metadata is limited to 8 MiB, serialization to 64 MiB. Actual model capacity and the existing 128000-token output reserve are checked separately. Text uses the declared conservative UTF-8 byte bound; image accounting is an explicit size estimate. Select a smaller complete scope or an explicit coverage plan; do not silently discard needed premises or lower the model policy.
guide.intervene.title: 6. Pause, continue and make decisions
guide.intervene.1: Pause stops new dispatch and preserves in-flight requests and captured responses. It does not undo a request already sent. Inspect Tasks & configuration and the remaining call budget before Continue existing work. Continue uses the existing authorization and balance; it does not refill the budget.
guide.intervene.2: End round is an explicit researcher's decision. The instance becomes ENDED; further research needs a new explicitly authorized instance. A report is a prerequisite only when you selected the report-first condition. No missing report should otherwise prevent you from retaining an honest open result or ending research.
guide.trw.title: 7. TRW example: sum of the first n odd numbers
guide.trw.1: Choose New project → TRW. Set project name to Odd-number sum and instance name to Induction proof. Paste the problem below, create the paused project, then open Start research round. Use the intent: Try induction, check n=1 and the step n to n+1, preserve the positive-integer domain and report every remaining gap.
guide.trw.input:
Prove that for every positive integer n,
1 + 3 + 5 + ... + (2n - 1) = n^2.
State the domain and summation convention explicitly.
A finite list of examples does not prove the universal statement.
guide.trw.2: After authorizing a finite round, inspect the argument in Current knowledge and the actual independent tasks in Tasks & configuration. The teaching reference is: 1=1², and n²+(2n+1)=(n+1)². Check the exact review scope and any open obligations. These reference calculations are not a record of a model run or a promise that a particular budget completes the proof.
guide.trw.3: When a formal deliverable is useful, click Make research report. TRW reports have lecture and minimal versions. Inspect both their semantic checks and actual page checks. You may pause, continue or end according to the actual result and your authorization.
guide.tfdw.title: 8. TFDW example: divisibility of consecutive-integer sums
guide.tfdw.1: Choose New project → TFDW. Name the project Consecutive integers and the instance Find divisibility conditions. Fill the three fields below separately. Start a finite round with this intent: Construct positive and negative examples, compare odd and even lengths, propose exact candidates and retain unknown comparisons.
guide.tfdw.input:
Phenomenon: 1+2+3=6 is divisible by 3; 1+2+3+4=10 is not divisible by 4; 1+2+3+4+5=15 is divisible by 5. What changes with the starting integer and length?

Immutable background: a is an integer; n is a positive integer; S(a,n)=a+(a+1)+...+(a+n-1). Divisibility means integer divisibility.

Allowed scope: vary a and n; compare odd/even n and seek necessary and sufficient conditions. Preserve consecutive integers and integer divisibility.
guide.tfdw.2: Read full candidates, counterevidence and unchecked comparisons in Candidates & handoff. A teaching candidate to inspect is: n divides S(a,n) exactly when n is odd, since S(a,n)/n=a+(n-1)/2. This calculation is a reference for inspection, not an executed PMRS result. The workflow may honestly return no candidate.
guide.tfdw.3: To select a candidate for proof, click Adopt as a new theorem research instance, read its exact full statement, and confirm Adopt and create paused TRW. Select that new instance and authorize its research separately. Adoption preserves the original TFDW and grants no proof qualification.
guide.survey.title: 9. Survey example: finite geometric sums
guide.survey.1: Choose Explore a new topic and Knowledge only. Set topic to Finite geometric sums over the real numbers; question to the exact formula including q=1; objects to real q and positive integer n. Include the finite sum, q≠1 formula, q=1 boundary and multiply-and-subtract proof. Exclude infinite series, convergence, matrices and historical priority claims. Create the paused instance.
guide.survey.input:
SYNTHETIC TEACHING MATERIAL — not a publication.
Let n be a positive integer and q a real number.
G_n(q)=1+q+...+q^(n-1).
For q!=1, (1-q)G_n(q)=1-q^n, so G_n(q)=(1-q^n)/(1-q).
For q=1, G_n(1)=n; division by 1-q is not allowed.
Multiply by q, align and subtract the two finite sums. Check n=1.
No claim about infinite-series convergence is made.
guide.survey.2: Save the labelled teaching text and upload it with Add materials. Open Start research round, select that source in Materials for this round (optional selection), and set the intent: “Read only the labelled finite-sum teaching source; organize the definition, q≠1 formula, separate q=1 case and proof; retain exact locations and unchecked scope.” Authorize a finite call limit. The normal entry advances necessary reading, organization and independent readiness work without separate S2/S3/S4 authorizations. Inspect the actual records in Survey knowledge & outputs; if material or a choice is missing, supply that specific input. A snapshot alone is not readiness or proof.
guide.survey.3: Knowledge only can deliver the selected knowledge without a manuscript. For later writing, create a linked paused instance with Write from existing knowledge or Update an existing survey. Select Survey manuscript and recheck the reused scope. If further reading, organization or review is needed, explicitly authorize Start research round in that linked instance and inspect actual readiness. Freeze selected knowledge, choose a minimal output plan, audience and perspective, and list proof commitments, required steps, omissions and limitations. Save English output plan makes no model call. After S5 output-budget authorization, Request selected English manuscript starts only that saved edition. Thematic and lecture are separate choices.
guide.survey.4: To continue mathematical research, use Hand off current workflow. For TRW select an exact statement and its necessary context. For TFDW provide the phenomenon, immutable background and allowed variation. Confirm the handoff, switch to the new paused instance, inspect its inherited materials, then authorize new research. Survey readiness or adoption does not certify the new target.
guide.reports.title: 10. Reports, drafts and unchanged-request recovery
guide.reports.1: Make research report explicitly requests TRW/TFDW lecture and minimal reports under available authorization. Survey uses the one saved output plan you selected. Each author, semantic-review and visual-review request consumes its authorized call allowance. A PDF alone is not a completed report: exact content, semantic review and every generated page must agree.
guide.reports.2: If rendering waits for memory or disk, free the resource and continue the same report. Its accepted body is retained and does not need another author call merely to render again. If relevant research changes after a report snapshot was frozen, STALE_CANDIDATE preserves that report; inspect the change and explicitly request a new report. The application does not silently replace its snapshot.
guide.reports.3: A manuscript objection about new mathematics creates open research work; prose or layout changes need the appropriate fresh checks. A failed revised draft cannot inherit the old draft's delivery status. Research reports shows current classification and missing checks; keep original responses and report versions while resolving the specific issue.
guide.trouble.title: 11. When work waits or something fails
guide.trouble.dependencies.meaning: A required upstream result, review or human selection is not available.
guide.trouble.dependencies.next: Inspect Open questions and pending duties. Supply the specific missing input or make the requested choice; do not declare the dependency complete from a saved file.
guide.trouble.resources.meaning: Preparation, a model slot, admission or rendering is temporarily unavailable.
guide.trouble.resources.next: Inspect the stated reason. Let occupied slots finish or free space on the affected filesystem, then continue/recover the original request. Do not create a replacement for an uncertain send.
guide.trouble.budget.meaning: Existing requests and reservations have used the authorized allowance.
guide.trouble.budget.next: Read the partial results and open work. Pause or end, or explicitly Authorize more calls in this round with a finite amount and reason. Saving the authorization does not start execution; Continue existing work does. Higher concurrency alone adds no calls.
guide.trouble.context.meaning: Necessary material plus instructions and output reserve cannot fit the supported request.
guide.trouble.context.next: Select a smaller complete scope or an explicit coverage plan, keeping required premises. Check exact model capability settings. Do not remove evidence or lower the output reserve silently.
guide.trouble.capture.meaning: The original response already exists; admission did not finish.
guide.trouble.capture.next: After freeing the stated resource, use Admit captured result to read the original capture without another model call. A contract defect may require the explicit repair path shown by the application; recovery alone cannot turn invalid content into a valid result. While paused, the capture stays retained for continuation.
guide.trouble.unknown.meaning: It is uncertain whether the original request was sent or completed.
guide.trouble.unknown.next: Use Resolve unknown request. Abandon waiting retains UNKNOWN and consumption. Confirm not sent requires actual external evidence. Refreshing or an explanatory note is not such evidence.
guide.trouble.receipt.state: A button was submitted but its reply was lost
guide.trouble.receipt.meaning: The original workspace operation may already have completed.
guide.trouble.receipt.next: Use the operation-recovery notice to query/recover its receipt. A completed result is restored; PENDING is not automatically resubmitted. Only an explicitly identified new operation gets a new key.
guide.trouble.report.meaning: Its frozen research changed, a check is missing, or a specific render/review step failed.
guide.trouble.report.next: Inspect the exact report and missing-check list. Retry temporary rendering on the same body; explicitly request a new snapshot only when the research scope changed. New scientific defects return to research.
guide.save.title: 12. Save, reopen and exit
guide.save.1: Native changes are stored as operations complete. Export backup creates a portable native archive. Restore backup checks an archive and creates a new paused project; it does not resume old processes automatically. Keep the originals, captured responses and receipts with the project.
guide.save.2: Closing a browser window is not Pause and does not stop the background service. Reopen PMRS from Applications and choose the same workspace. To stop the service, first Pause research, wait for in-flight work to finish, then use Quit background service. Reopening, changing the port or refreshing does not authorize duplicate requests.
guide.demo.note: The buttons below open separate deterministic simulation projects. Their responses are test fixtures with no real model calls and are not evidence that your mathematical problem is solved. The three worked inputs above are teaching examples you may inspect before authorizing real work.
guide.start.4: For TRW, normal start checks whether valid background and notation (P1), reverse analysis of the target (P2), and route exploration (P3) already exist for these inputs. It reuses applicable work and schedules missing responsibilities. Actual results, proposed concrete gaps and dependencies then drive necessary research and return work within this same finite authorization. You do not need to click each stage, and normal start does not always begin at P4.
guide.start.5: TFDW develops evidence, candidates, distinguishing work and independent formulation checks, then presents the candidate frontier for your choice. Survey reads the selected material, organizes knowledge and checks readiness as needed. Missing source material or knowledge causes a visible request for input; normal start does not silently retrieve online sources. Knowledge only does not start manuscript writing.
guide.start.6: The workflow does not run every stage just to fill a checklist. Relevant non-independent duties may share a contract when their actual work remains traceable; independent checks and true dependencies stay separate. Host scheduling, input selection and bookkeeping make no model calls. A new branch or return consumes the original remaining allowance, not a new hidden budget.
guide.observe.4: This round: progress and next decision shows actual new records, unfinished and unperformed duties, links to original bodies, and open questions. At a stopping point, the P13-style account preserves achievements, failures and gaps for your P14 decision. A call limit reached, a resource wait, a dependency wait, a fault and a ready handoff are different outcomes. A deliverable may remain mathematically open; the system does not open a new round or decide your next research goal.
guide.intervene.3: To change a specific piece of work, choose Request a correction. Select Affected responsibility, including an existing task or an unfrozen duty; fill Specific issue and correction and Success criterion. Save correction and pause records an executable responsibility in the same round and stops new dispatch. An affected task not yet sent is held; sent requests and captures retain their identity. Continue existing work first recovers eligible original captures, then handles the correction within the remaining budget.
guide.intervene.4: Example correction: “The argument divided by 1-q without separating q=1.” Success criterion: “State q≠1 before division; prove G_n(1)=n separately; retain n≥1 and identify which revised claims need fresh review.” Inspect the resulting task and full response, not only the saved correction message.
guide.survey.5: For a concrete Survey → TRW handoff, choose the exact saved statement “For real q and positive integer n, G_n(q)=(1-q^n)/(1-q) when q≠1; G_n(1)=n” with its required context. For Survey → TFDW, use the phenomenon that the quotient formula has a removable-looking boundary at q=1, keep real q and positive integer n fixed, and permit comparing only finite-sum algebraic formulations. Neither handoff authorizes a new call. Inspect the new paused instance and explicitly Start research round.
guide.save.3: Keep enough space for the workspace and PDF renderer temporary directory. Disposable preparation copies may be reclaimed after a response is sealed and settled; that does not delete original sources, captures, receipts or report evidence. Export a backup before moving the project and verify the restored paused copy before authorizing it.
guide.intervene.5: When the original allowance is exhausted, use Authorize more calls in this round. Fill Additional calls (1–1000) and Reason for additional authorization, then Save authorization without starting. The explicit increase preserves the original round, scope, concurrency, frozen requests and cumulative responsibility-attempt limits. Click Continue existing work separately to resume recorded corrections and other eligible work. A new round is for a new purpose; extra calls do not bypass attempt limits or missing dependencies.
guide.assistant.title: 13. Project assistant: diagnose and revise a report
guide.assistant.1: Open Project assistant in the project toolbar. Ask about this issue on a task and Discuss or revise this report on a manuscript open the same panel with an exact context. Check the displayed project, workflow instance, task/request, report edition and revision. The general entry restores the last conversation; New conversation in this project starts a separate history. Switching the workbench project does not move the open conversation.
guide.assistant.2: The assistant uses gpt-6-astra with Extra high reasoning. Its initial allowance is zero. Enter Additional assistant calls (suggested 3), then Authorize assistant calls without sending. Each sent turn permits one assistant call; reading history, refreshing status and opening evidence make no model call. Assistant and report allowances are separate from research authorization. A report revision does not resume paused research.
guide.assistant.3: For a diagnosis, describe what you see and the decision you need. The reply distinguishes confirmed facts, inferences, unknowns and suggested steps, with evidence references and collection time. A stored status is not proof of a currently live process. Login failure, unavailable model or missing evidence remains an explicit limitation; use Settings & sign-in or this Guide when the assistant cannot answer.
guide.assistant.diagnose: Why is this task waiting? Explain the actual evidence and what I need to do next. Do not change any report or resume research.
guide.assistant.4: For a manuscript, open Discuss or revise this report on the exact edition. Read the listed section titles and discussed revision first. A question, discussion, or “do not modify” instruction only analyzes. A clear instruction with a valid exact target and scope can start native revision when report allowance is available; there is no extra confirmation merely to repeat that authorization. Missing target, unclear section, changed version or absent allowance requires the specific missing input.
guide.assistant.revise:
First message: Explain what is unclear in Section 3; do not modify the report yet.
After reading the diagnosis: Revise only Section 3 of this selected report. Define each symbol before use, preserve the mathematical domain and assumptions, and leave all other sections unchanged.
Follow-up: Please revise only Section 3 again, keeping those requirements. Also separate the q=1 case before division by 1-q. Do not introduce new mathematical claims.
guide.assistant.5: Use Effective revision requirements to inspect accumulated user constraints. Later messages do not erase earlier requirements silently. For a local section revision, unselected source bytes are preserved. Whole-report changes require a whole-report instruction. New mathematical research, assumptions, proof qualification or changed workflow scope needs its own native decision and is not silently performed by the assistant.
guide.assistant.6: Authorize report calls for this request (optional) is a separate finite amount for authors and reviewers. Leave it blank to use an applicable existing report allowance. If the original turn is waiting for report allowance, fill this field and click Continue the original request on that turn: it does not need a new assistant inference. The shared host pool and project concurrency still apply. A queued revision is not finished; inspect Native report processing, actual semantic review, rendered status and recorded page reviews. Earlier and revised PDFs are separate links only when those files exist.
guide.assistant.7: A temporary resource wait retains the original request. A captured reply awaiting admission is recovered from the same bytes. UNKNOWN means the original send outcome is uncertain and is never automatically resent. If a submission reply is lost, use the original-operation recovery notice instead of submitting the message again. Render or review failure keeps the body, earlier versions and actual missing checks; it does not inherit the old delivery status.
guide.assistant.8: Conversation history survives reopening. View evidence summary reads a bounded local summary; Download diagnostic summary saves it for your review and does not upload it. The summary does not automatically include full manuscripts or the research library. Closing the panel or browser does not cancel a sent assistant/report job and does not pause research. Reopen the same conversation to inspect its original outcome.
